gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-phoenician: Commanding and a bit playful, Righteous bends every stroke like thin steel rod, with bowls that fill the line. But Noto Sans Phoenician is the one with the modern lowercase, tall and generous, with s curves that open wide at both ends.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-psalter-pahla: Righteous looks like one thin steel rod bent into letters, with bowls that fill the line and no hairline joins anywhere. And Noto Sans Psalter Pahlavi supplies the approachable counterweight, its e mouths gaping and its capitals barely rising.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-rejang: Noto Sans Rejang reads openly, its lowercase counters like wide glass portholes. Righteous sits above in stems that match its hairlines, because it has none, so the heading looks cut from wire while the sans text below stays full of daylight.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-runic: Chunky, bendy, wire-thin lettering with attitude. Righteous is best at looking thin without any thinner parts at all, while Noto Sans Runic does its best work with a big x-height and curves that never close back on themselves.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Noto Sans Samaritan has a hefty lowercase and curves with plenty of daylight inside, so it feels approachable from the first line. And Righteous, ending every stroke at the same measured thickness, keeps the headline bold while this plain sans carries the reading along comfortably.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-sc: Righteous looks like sign-shop vinyl cut to a single line width, with bowls that fill the line. Noto Sans SC is the quiet partner, its chalk curves stopping well short of closing.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-sharada: Noto Sans Sharada keeps its c forms open and its lowercase bulky. Righteous brings the real strength here, tails and terminals as thick as the stems, so the heading hits hard while the sans text stays clean.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-siddham: Righteous builds its uppercase from lines of one constant thickness, like thin steel rod bent into shape, with bowls that fill the line. But Noto Sans Siddham settles into a large central band in the text, and its s ends hang far from the spine, which feels friendly over a long passage.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-sinhala: Commanding, thin-skeleton lettering up top gives way to something far denser. Righteous holds one fixed stroke thickness while the plain sans Noto Sans Sinhala lays a dark stripe of lowercase through every line, its curve endings keeping well apart.
gen-righteous-gf-noto-sans-soyombo: Wirelike strokes, fun and commanding, bowls filling the line. Noto Sans Soyombo is the sturdy part, with a sizable x-height made for screen reading and curved letters with wide, unclosed mouths.
